body: A write-ahead log persists each accepted change before memory is updated. After a crash, replay reconstructs inserts, updates, deletes, and the latest document versions.
title: Crash recovery with a write-ahead log

body: A deletion tombstone masks an obsolete baseline copy immediately. Query processing excludes the old version until compaction physically omits it from a new baseline generation.
title: Tombstones and deleted search documents

body: Compaction captures a high-water sequence, materializes current live documents, validates results, and atomically activates a new immutable baseline. Later events remain in the delta.
title: Index compaction and high-water marks

body: BM25 ranks documents using exact query terms, term frequency, inverse document frequency, and document-length normalization. It is strong for rare identifiers and precise vocabulary.
title: Lexical retrieval with BM25

body: Dense retrieval embeds queries and documents into a shared vector space. Similar meanings can be close even when the query and document do not use identical words.
title: Semantic retrieval with embeddings

body: HNSW is an approximate nearest-neighbor graph. Connectivity and construction expansion affect memory, build cost, recall, while search expansion controls the query latency and recall tradeoff.
title: Tuning an HNSW vector index

body: Reciprocal Rank Fusion combines lexical and dense rankings with reciprocal rank contributions. It avoids adding incompatible BM25 and cosine score scales directly.
title: Hybrid search using reciprocal rank fusion

body: Typed metadata filters restrict candidates by fields such as region, publication year, tenant, or category. Dense search expands its candidate window until enough eligible results are found.
title: Filtered lexical and vector retrieval

body: Replicated logs and serving replicas provide availability after a machine failure. Leader election and fencing prevent two writers from assigning conflicting operation order.
title: Replication and failover for search services

body: Search observability includes query latency percentiles, update freshness, replay throughput, compaction duration, index size, error counters, and deleted-result leakage alerts.
title: Monitoring a retrieval service
